sourceVersion: NIST SP 800-86 (2006) with clearly labeled modern supplements

categories.title: Forensic Readiness
categories.description: Ensure systems and personnel are prepared to preserve and collect digital evidence effectively.

categories.title: Collection
categories.description: Acquire volatile and non-volatile evidence while maintaining an unbroken chain of custody.

categories.title: Examination
categories.description: Extract, verify, and normalize forensic artifacts without altering original evidence.

categories.title: Analysis
categories.description: Correlate artifacts across sources to test hypotheses and reconstruct adversary actions.

categories.title: Reporting
categories.description: Document findings, executive impact, technical indicators, and remediation steps.

categories.title: Files and filesystems
categories.description: Analyze partition tables, filesystems, deleted files, unallocated space, and volume snapshots.

categories.title: Operating systems and volatile data
categories.description: Extract process listings, injected code, network sockets, credentials, and console history from RAM.

categories.title: Network traffic
categories.description: Inspect packet captures, DNS queries, C2 beaconing patterns, and payload transfers.

categories.title: Windows artifacts
categories.description: Examine Windows registry hives, event logs, MFT/USN records, and execution artifacts.

categories.title: Linux artifacts
categories.description: Inspect Linux authentication logs, cron jobs, shell history, and persistence mechanisms.

categories.title: Applications and logs
categories.description: Aggregate and analyze web server, authentication, and application log streams.

categories.title: Malware triage
categories.description: Perform static triage, string analysis, and behavioral extraction on suspicious binaries.

nodes.title: Establish Forensic Readiness
nodes.goal: Establish policy, authority, roles, privacy safeguards, retention, logging, and a tested forensic capability before an incident.
nodes.why: Evidence is more useful when sources, ownership, procedures, constraints, and responsibilities are known in advance.
checklist: Define who authorizes forensic work and how incident response, legal, privacy, HR, and system owners coordinate.
Inventory likely evidence sources, owners, time sources, retention periods, access controls, encryption, and collection constraints.
Document evidence handling, chain of custody, secure storage, disposal, and escalation procedures.
Maintain a trusted toolkit, validate it on representative systems, and train personnel on its capabilities and side effects.
lookFor: Unowned sources
Retention or telemetry gaps
Unclear authority
Untested tools
nodes.record: Record the readiness owner, approved procedures, evidence inventory, retention decisions, tool-validation results, exercise date, and unresolved gaps.
cautions: Coordinate legal and privacy requirements with qualified organizational counsel; this guide does not determine admissibility or collection authority.

nodes.title: Validate tooling, telemetry & time sources
nodes.goal: Confirm collection tools, logging, clocks, and storage support repeatable forensic work.
nodes.why: Tool behavior, missing logs, clock drift, and insufficient storage can limit later examination and correlation.
checklist: Test trusted tools on representative systems and document changes they make.
Verify time synchronization and preserve timezone and clock-offset context.
Exercise log export, evidence transfer, access control, backup, and recovery.
Track tool versions and prepare alternate collection methods for critical sources.
lookFor: Clock drift
Collection-induced changes
Disabled audit sources
Insufficient retention
nodes.record: Record tool name, version, validation case, observed side effects, clock source, telemetry coverage, retention period, and corrective owner.
cautions: A validated tool can still alter a live system; assess and document its expected impact for each use.

nodes.title: Preserve digital evidence & chain of custody
nodes.goal: Prioritize and acquire relevant data while preserving integrity, provenance, and accountable custody.
nodes.why: Collection choices affect availability and completeness; they are documented risk decisions, not universal actions.
checklist: Build an acquisition plan ordered by likely value, volatility, and amount of effort.
Document system identity, physical and logical state, location, connections, current time, timezone, and custodian.
Choose containment or isolation based on incident risk, operational impact, authority, and evidence-loss risk; do not disconnect by default.
Use trusted methods, record every transfer, calculate SHA-256, secure the master copy, and examine a verified working copy.
lookFor: Volatile data at risk
Encryption or remote-destruction risk
Alternative sources
Collection errors
nodes.record: Record acquisition priorities and rationale, authority, source identifiers, system state, tool/version, commands, timestamps, handlers, errors, storage, and SHA-256 values.
cautions: Containment, shutdown, and live collection can alter or destroy evidence; make and document a case-specific risk decision.

findings.title: Live system running with volatile memory

nodes.title: Live system triage & memory acquisition
nodes.goal: Collect relevant volatile data in an order justified by likely value, volatility, and collection effort.
nodes.why: RAM contains encryption keys, injected memory payloads, decrypted network communications, and process states that are lost upon reboot or shutdown.
checklist: Record system time, timezone, clock offset, logged-in users, and operator.
Choose and document a case-specific order for network state, processes, open files, configuration, and memory.
Use trusted minimal-footprint tools and capture name, version, source, output, errors, and side effects.
Hash and transfer outputs to controlled storage, retaining a protected master and verified working copy.
lookFor: Live RAM capture files, unusual background processes, remote management tunnels, and uncommitted cryptographic material.
nodes.record: Record the volatility order and rationale, command sequence, start/end times, tool impact, errors, output paths, hashes, and custody transfers.
cautions: Do not apply a fixed volatility order mechanically; balance evidence value and loss risk against operational impact.

nodes.title: Forensic dead-box disk imaging & hashing
nodes.goal: Create bit-stream forensic images (E01 / raw DD) of non-volatile storage media using hardware write blockers and cryptographic verification.
nodes.why: Bit-stream images capture allocated data, unallocated clusters, slack space, and partition metadata without modifying the original source disk.
checklist: Confirm source identity and document write-blocker make, model, and validation.
Create a bit-stream image when in scope and record unreadable sectors, retries, and settings.
Use SHA-256 as the primary integrity digest; record MD5 only for required legacy interoperability.
Secure the master image and examine a verified working copy.
lookFor: Bit-for-bit hash match between physical drive and forensic image, bad sector logs, and hidden host protected areas (HPA/DCO).
nodes.record: Record device identifiers, format, tool/version, write blocker, times, errors, source and image SHA-256, master location, and working-copy verification.
cautions: A matching digest supports integrity but does not alone establish provenance, completeness, or a legal conclusion.

nodes.title: Verify evidence integrity & triage preparation
nodes.goal: Prepare and examine verified working copies while preserving source context.
nodes.why: Working directly on original evidence or unverified duplicates risks contamination and invalidates forensic conclusions.
checklist: Verify the working copy against its documented SHA-256 and preserve the master.
Document tools, versions, settings, errors, and limitations.
Extract relevant data without losing source paths, offsets, and timestamp context.
Validate material results with an alternate tool or method when practical.
lookFor: Verification hash match, volume encryption status (BitLocker, LUKS, APFS), and partition boundary anomalies.
nodes.record: Record input hash, working-copy identifier, tool/version, settings, searches, extracted-item provenance, validation, errors, and excluded data.
cautions: Tool output interprets source data; retain provenance and independently check material results.

nodes.title: Super-timeline generation & event extraction
nodes.goal: Extract normalized chronological event records across filesystem MACB timestamps, system logs, registry hives, and application artifacts.
nodes.why: Super-timelines correlate disparate events into a single unified temporal stream, exposing attacker activity before and after an incident.
checklist: Run log2timeline / Plaso parsers against mounted disk images, registry hives, and event logs.
Normalize all parsed timestamps to UTC and filter by target incident time windows.
Extract MACB (Modified, Accessed, Changed, Born) metadata from filesystem master records.
Generate indexed CSV/database timeline exports for targeted querying.
lookFor: Time clusters of file creation, rapid timestamp modifications (timestomping), user login spikes, and service creation events.
nodes.record: Record super-timeline generation & event extraction inputs, source locators, original timestamps and offsets, tool/version, settings, outputs, validation, errors, limitations, and hashes.
cautions: Maintain chain of custody; operate on verified read-only working copies and avoid altering original evidence.

nodes.title: Multi-source correlation & attack attribution
nodes.goal: Correlate observations across sources to test what is supported, contradicted, or unresolved.
nodes.why: One artifact can have benign or malicious explanations; conclusions require context and corroboration.
checklist: Normalize timestamps with documented timezone and clock-offset context.
State the primary hypothesis and plausible alternative hypotheses, including authorized explanations.
Distinguish observations from inferences and grade conclusions by source quality and independence.
Seek contradictory evidence and label results inconclusive when evidence cannot discriminate.
lookFor: Correlated timeline sequences linking initial vector, privilege escalation, credential dumping, lateral movement, and data staging.
nodes.record: Record each hypothesis, supporting and contradicting artifacts, provenance, time choices, assumptions, confidence, alternatives, and unresolved questions.
cautions: Do not infer identity, intent, or causation from one artifact; state uncertainty and competing explanations.

findings.title: Malicious binary or persistence payload detected

nodes.title: Determine root cause, dwell time & scope of compromise
nodes.goal: Identify initial access vectors, determine adversary dwell time, quantify affected systems and sensitive data exposure, and evaluate business impact.
nodes.why: Complete impact scoping prevents premature remediation that leaves adversary backdoors or unmonitored persistence active in the environment.
checklist: Trace the earliest adversary artifact to establish incident start time and calculate dwell duration.
Identify the initial vulnerability, stolen credential, or phishing payload enabling perimeter breach.
Catalog all compromised endpoints, service accounts, and elevated privileges accessed during the intrusion.
Assess exfiltrated or tampered data assets against regulatory notification thresholds.
lookFor: First entry timestamp, exploited CVE details, compromised account list, exfiltration staging folders, and total blast radius.
nodes.record: Record determine root cause, dwell time & scope of compromise inputs, source locators, original timestamps and offsets, tool/version, settings, outputs, validation, errors, limitations, and hashes.
cautions: Maintain chain of custody; operate on verified read-only working copies and avoid altering original evidence.

nodes.title: Executive findings summary & incident timeline
nodes.goal: Communicate verified facts, qualified conclusions, impact, limitations, and actionable leads for the audience.
nodes.why: Executives need clear, non-jargon summaries to make risk management, legal, and operational business decisions during and after an incident.
checklist: Identify the audience and separate executive decisions from technical detail.
Summarize scope, methods, timeline, impact, confidence, and material alternatives.
State evidence gaps, assumptions, tool or collection limitations, and inconclusive questions.
Provide actionable leads and conduct a process review.
lookFor: Clear executive narrative, quantified impact metrics, regulatory disclosure implications, and decision milestones.
nodes.record: Record audience, scope, evidence identifiers, methods, facts, qualified conclusions, confidence, limitations, unresolved questions, actions, reviewer, and version.
cautions: Avoid legal conclusions and absolute attribution; trace every material claim to preserved evidence and documented analysis.

nodes.title: Technical forensics report & IOC documentation
nodes.goal: Document reproducible forensic methodology, artifact locations, tool outputs, and comprehensive Indicator of Compromise (IOC) tables.
nodes.why: Technical reports serve as definitive evidentiary records for legal proceedings, peer review, and engineering remediation teams.
checklist: Document evidence identification, forensic tool versions, command invocations, and cryptographic hashes.
Detail step-by-step artifact findings with raw logs, memory dumps, and file offsets.
Compile structured IOC tables (file hashes, C2 IP addresses, domains, registry keys, YARA rules).
Include comprehensive timeline appendix detailing every correlated event.
lookFor: Complete chain of evidence, reproducible technical findings, validated IOC lists, and artifact references.
nodes.record: Record scope, authority, evidence inventory, custody, methods, hashes, provenance, time normalization, findings, limitations, and peer-review changes.
cautions: Make the report reproducible without exposing sensitive evidence beyond the authorized audience.

nodes.title: Remediation guidance & lessons learned
nodes.goal: Provide actionable eradication steps, strategic defensive hardening recommendations, and lessons-learned improvements per NIST SP 800-61r3.
nodes.why: Post-incident reviews strengthen enterprise defenses, close exploited architectural gaps, and improve future incident response efficiency.
checklist: Detail complete eradication requirements (account credential resets, system rebuilds, backdoor removal).
Propose tactical controls (endpoint detection rules, firewall blocks, EDR telemetry gaps).
Propose strategic controls (network segmentation, MFA enforcement, privileged access management).
Conduct a formal lessons-learned meeting and update incident response playbooks.
lookFor: Validated eradication checklists, detection engineering gaps, security control upgrades, and playbook updates.
nodes.record: Record remediation guidance & lessons learned inputs, source locators, original timestamps and offsets, tool/version, settings, outputs, validation, errors, limitations, and hashes.
cautions: Maintain chain of custody; operate on verified read-only working copies and avoid altering original evidence.

nodes.title: Verify disk image format & cryptographic hash
nodes.goal: Compute verification hashes (MD5, SHA-256) of raw or E01 disk images and inspect image metadata headers.
nodes.why: Ensures evidence integrity before analysis begins and prevents corrupted image processing.
checklist: Calculate SHA-256 checksum of disk image file and compare against custody documentation.
Identify forensic container format (Raw DD, E01 Expert Witness, VMDK, VHDX, QCOW2).
Inspect E01 header metadata (examiner name, case number, acquisition date, notes).
Mount image using read-only loopback or ewfmount.
lookFor: Hash match verification, corrupted sectors, compression artifacts, and container metadata details.
nodes.record: Record verify disk image format & cryptographic hash inputs, source locators, original timestamps and offsets, tool/version, settings, outputs, validation, errors, limitations, and hashes.
cautions: Maintain chain of custody; operate on verified read-only working copies and avoid altering original evidence.

nodes.title: Identify partition tables & volume systems
nodes.goal: Parse MBR, GPT, or volume manager headers to locate active partitions, unallocated gaps, and hidden volume structures.
nodes.why: Attackers and malware can conceal data in unallocated sectors between partitions or unpartitioned disk space.
checklist: Run 'mmls' to parse Master Boot Record (MBR) or GUID Partition Table (GPT) layouts.
Calculate sector offsets and cluster sizes for each partition.
Identify unallocated gaps between partition boundaries and volume slack.
Check for dynamic disks, LVM physical volumes, or encrypted BitLocker/LUKS volumes.
lookFor: Partition sector offsets, hidden non-standard partition types, large unpartitioned space gaps, and volume headers.
nodes.record: Record identify partition tables & volume systems inputs, source locators, original timestamps and offsets, tool/version, settings, outputs, validation, errors, limitations, and hashes.
cautions: Maintain chain of custody; operate on verified read-only working copies and avoid altering original evidence.

nodes.title: Enumerate filesystem metadata & directory tree
nodes.goal: Traverse directory structures, timestamps, file allocations, and metadata structures (inodes/MFT records) without altering data.
nodes.why: Directory enumeration provides baseline filesystem layout and maps user profiles, application data, and system configurations.
checklist: Run 'fls' with partition sector offset to list directory trees recursively.
Inspect filesystem statistics ('fsstat') to determine cluster size, total blocks, and metadata layout.
Identify abnormal directory structures, hidden files, and unauthorized executable paths.
Document filesystem type (NTFS, FAT32, exFAT, EXT4, APFS, XFS).
lookFor: Unusually placed binaries, hidden folders, non-standard system files, and suspicious user directory additions.
nodes.record: Record enumerate filesystem metadata & directory tree inputs, source locators, original timestamps and offsets, tool/version, settings, outputs, validation, errors, limitations, and hashes.
cautions: Maintain chain of custody; operate on verified read-only working copies and avoid altering original evidence.

nodes.title: Recover deleted files & analyze unallocated space
nodes.goal: Extract deleted directory entries, trace unallocated clusters, and extract orphaned file records using filesystem metadata.
nodes.why: Attackers regularly delete staging tools, payloads, and exfiltration archives to cover tracks.
checklist: Use 'fls -r -d' to list deleted directory entries and orphaned metadata pointers.
Extract deleted files using 'icat' pointing to inode or MFT record numbers.
Inspect filesystem journal files ($LogFile, ext4 journal) for recent transaction rollbacks.
Export raw unallocated blocks using 'blkls' for subsequent deep carving.
lookFor: Deleted executables, temporary batch scripts, PowerShell scripts, staging ZIP archives, and log wipe residue.
nodes.record: Record recover deleted files & analyze unallocated space inputs, source locators, original timestamps and offsets, tool/version, settings, outputs, validation, errors, limitations, and hashes.
cautions: Maintain chain of custody; operate on verified read-only working copies and avoid altering original evidence.

nodes.title: File carving via magic bytes & headers
nodes.goal: Reconstruct contiguous and fragmented files from raw unallocated disk blocks using magic byte signatures and structural validators.
nodes.why: File carving recovers critical evidence when filesystem metadata records have been wiped or overwritten.
checklist: Run Foremost or PhotoRec against unallocated raw space ('blkls' output).
Configure custom headers/footers for proprietary file formats, custom logs, or binary payloads.
Run Binwalk to detect embedded files, compressed archives, and firmware components.
Validate integrity of carved files against expected format parsers.
lookFor: Carved PE executables, ZIP archives, Office documents, PDFs, certificates, and SQLite databases.
nodes.record: Record file carving via magic bytes & headers inputs, source locators, original timestamps and offsets, tool/version, settings, outputs, validation, errors, limitations, and hashes.
cautions: Maintain chain of custody; operate on verified read-only working copies and avoid altering original evidence.

findings.title: Executable binary carved from unallocated space

nodes.title: Bulk feature extraction & keyword search
nodes.goal: Rapidly scan raw volume blocks for email addresses, URLs, IP addresses, private keys, and high-entropy secrets.
nodes.why: Feature extraction bypasses filesystem complexity to locate actionable indicators of compromise in seconds.
checklist: Run Bulk Extractor against raw disk image or unallocated blocks.
Extract and aggregate IP addresses, domain names, and URLs into triage lists.
Extract email addresses, credit card numbers, and cryptographic private keys.
Perform targeted keyword searches for known project names, credentials, or malware strings.
lookFor: Attacker C2 IP addresses, staging URLs, leaked passwords, API tokens, and user credentials.
nodes.record: Record bulk feature extraction & keyword search inputs, source locators, original timestamps and offsets, tool/version, settings, outputs, validation, errors, limitations, and hashes.
cautions: Maintain chain of custody; operate on verified read-only working copies and avoid altering original evidence.

nodes.title: Inspect Volume Shadow Copies & snapshot deltas
nodes.goal: Mount and parse historical VSS snapshots to analyze past configurations, recover overwritten files, and track ransomware timing.
nodes.why: Shadow copies preserve historical states of files, registry hives, and system binaries from before adversary tampering or encryption.
checklist: Enumerate available Volume Shadow Copies using vshadowinfo / libvshadow.
Mount shadow copy snapshots as independent read-only filesystems.
Compare file modifications and registry keys between historical snapshots and current disk state.
Extract historical copies of SAM, SYSTEM, and NTUSER.DAT hives.
lookFor: Pre-encryption file copies, historical malware configurations, deleted user accounts, and modified system binaries.
nodes.record: Record inspect volume shadow copies & snapshot deltas inputs, source locators, original timestamps and offsets, tool/version, settings, outputs, validation, errors, limitations, and hashes.
cautions: Maintain chain of custody; operate on verified read-only working copies and avoid altering original evidence.

nodes.title: Identify memory profile & kernel architecture
nodes.goal: Determine OS build, kernel symbols, ASLR base, and DTB (Directory Table Base) from volatile memory dump.
nodes.why: Accurate memory symbol resolution is required to parse kernel structures, processes, and memory objects.
checklist: Run Volatility 3 banner / isfinfo to determine OS version, kernel build, and architecture.
Verify memory dump format (raw physical RAM, crash dump, ELF core, VMware .vmem, Hyper-V).
Download or generate intermediate symbol tables (ISF) matching target kernel.
Document memory size, acquisition tool signature, and DTB pointer.
lookFor: Kernel version, build number, processor architecture (x86/x64/ARM), and symbol matching status.
nodes.record: Record identify memory profile & kernel architecture inputs, source locators, original timestamps and offsets, tool/version, settings, outputs, validation, errors, limitations, and hashes.
cautions: Maintain chain of custody; operate on verified read-only working copies and avoid altering original evidence.

nodes.title: Enumerate process hierarchy & detect unlinked processes
nodes.goal: Compare ActiveProcessLinks (pslist) against memory pool scans (psscan) to detect DKOM hidden processes and abnormal parentage.
nodes.why: Rootkits and sophisticated malware detach process structures from active lists to hide from task managers and standard tools.
checklist: Run 'windows.pslist' to view the active doubly-linked list of processes.
Run 'windows.psscan' to find unlinked process blocks via memory pool signature scanning.
Run 'windows.pstree' to evaluate parent-child process relationships and verify expected parent PIDs.
Compare pslist vs psscan output to isolate unlinked hidden processes (DKOM).
lookFor: Mismatched process start/exit times, abnormal parent processes (e.g. cmd.exe spawned by spoolsv.exe), and processes with fake names.
nodes.record: Record enumerate process hierarchy & detect unlinked processes inputs, source locators, original timestamps and offsets, tool/version, settings, outputs, validation, errors, limitations, and hashes.
cautions: Maintain chain of custody; operate on verified read-only working copies and avoid altering original evidence.

nodes.title: Detect process injection & memory anomalies
nodes.goal: Identify injected DLLs, hollowed processes, RWX memory segments, and shellcode payloads using memory scanning.
nodes.why: Attackers inject malicious code into legitimate processes (svchost.exe, explorer.exe) to evade endpoint detection.
checklist: Run 'windows.malfind' to scan for executable (PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE) memory segments not backed by disk.
Inspect dumped memory regions for PE headers ('MZ' / 'PE' magic bytes) or shellcode NOP sleds.
Run 'windows.ldrmodules' to detect unlinked DLLs hidden from PEB loader data tables.
Dump suspicious injected memory sections using 'windows.dumpfiles'.
lookFor: Unbacked executable memory pages, reflective DLL injections, process hollowing indicators, and shellcode stubs.
nodes.record: Record detect process injection & memory anomalies inputs, source locators, original timestamps and offsets, tool/version, settings, outputs, validation, errors, limitations, and hashes.
cautions: Maintain chain of custody; operate on verified read-only working copies and avoid altering original evidence.

findings.title: Injected shellcode or hollowed PE dumped

nodes.title: Inspect memory network sockets & active connections
nodes.goal: Extract active TCP/UDP endpoints, historical closed sockets, and associated process PIDs from volatile memory structures.
nodes.why: Correlating memory network sockets with processes identifies C2 beacons, reverse shells, and unauthorized data exfiltration channels.
checklist: Run 'windows.netscan' or 'linux.sockscan' to enumerate active and closed network connections.
Correlate remote IP addresses and foreign ports with process PIDs and executable names.
Cross-reference remote IP addresses against threat intelligence and WHOIS data.
Check for listening ports associated with non-standard service processes.
lookFor: Suspicious outbound connections on non-standard ports, reverse shell connections, and connections from injected system processes.
nodes.record: Record inspect memory network sockets & active connections inputs, source locators, original timestamps and offsets, tool/version, settings, outputs, validation, errors, limitations, and hashes.
cautions: Maintain chain of custody; operate on verified read-only working copies and avoid altering original evidence.

nodes.title: Analyze kernel drivers, hooks & SSDT modifications
nodes.goal: Scan for unsigned kernel drivers, SSDT hooks, IRP table detours, and kernel-mode rootkit modifications.
nodes.why: Kernel rootkits manipulate core OS telemetry, hide files/processes from userland tools, and disable EDR agents.
checklist: Run 'windows.modules' / 'windows.driverscan' to list loaded kernel drivers.
Run 'windows.ssdt' to detect system service dispatch table hooking.
Check MajorFunction tables in driver objects for IRP hook detours.
Verify driver digital signatures and base addresses against known legitimate kernel modules.
lookFor: Hooked SSDT entries pointing outside ntoskrnl.exe address space, hidden drivers, and modified kernel code pages.
nodes.record: Record analyze kernel drivers, hooks & ssdt modifications inputs, source locators, original timestamps and offsets, tool/version, settings, outputs, validation, errors, limitations, and hashes.
cautions: Maintain chain of custody; operate on verified read-only working copies and avoid altering original evidence.

nodes.title: Extract cached credentials, keys & decrypted sessions
nodes.goal: Recover LSASS credentials, master keys, DPAPI keys, BitLocker recovery passwords, and decrypted TLS session data.
nodes.why: Identifies whether attacker harvested credentials to perform lateral movement or if credentials can be recovered for incident analysis.
checklist: Run 'windows.hashdump' and 'windows.cachedump' to extract SAM hashes and domain cached credentials.
Extract LSA secrets and Kerberos tickets from memory structures.
Scan for DPAPI master keys and BitLocker recovery keys.
Extract plaintext passwords from memory buffers of password managers or active browser sessions.
lookFor: Plaintext credentials, NTLM password hashes, Kerberos TGT/TGS tickets, and encryption keys.
nodes.record: Record extract cached credentials, keys & decrypted sessions inputs, source locators, original timestamps and offsets, tool/version, settings, outputs, validation, errors, limitations, and hashes.
cautions: Credential material is highly sensitive; minimize access, encrypt storage, and coordinate authorized rotation.

nodes.title: Recover command history & console buffers
nodes.goal: Reconstruct executed console commands, PowerShell sessions, and bash buffers from conhost/cmd memory structures.
nodes.why: Command line buffers reveal exact commands executed by attackers, downloaded scripts, and internal reconnaissance syntax.
checklist: Run 'windows.cmdline' to extract process command line arguments.
Inspect conhost.exe and cmd.exe process memory for active console input/output buffers.
Extract PowerShell execution logs, encoded script blocks, and piped command streams.
Extract environment variables associated with each process.
lookFor: Base64 encoded PowerShell commands ('-enc'), obfuscated cmd scripts, download cradles (IEX / WebClient), and reconnaissance commands (whoami, net view).
nodes.record: Record recover command history & console buffers inputs, source locators, original timestamps and offsets, tool/version, settings, outputs, validation, errors, limitations, and hashes.
cautions: Maintain chain of custody; operate on verified read-only working copies and avoid altering original evidence.

nodes.title: Initial PCAP triage & protocol hierarchy overview
nodes.goal: Analyze protocol distribution, conversation endpoints, packet volume spikes, and time bounds of network capture.
nodes.why: High-level PCAP triage scopes the capture timeframe, isolates high-volume streams, and pinpoints anomaly candidates.
checklist: Run 'tshark -q -z io,phs -r capture.pcap' to generate protocol hierarchy statistics.
Extract IP conversation summary with 'tshark -q -z conv,ip -r capture.pcap'.
Identify capture start and end timestamps and check for packet truncation (snaplen limits).
Filter broadcast and noise protocols (LLMNR, MDNS, SSDP, ARP) to isolate unicast sessions.
lookFor: Volume spikes, abnormal protocol distributions, large data transfers, and non-standard port usages.
nodes.record: Record initial pcap triage & protocol hierarchy overview inputs, source locators, original timestamps and offsets, tool/version, settings, outputs, validation, errors, limitations, and hashes.
cautions: Maintain chain of custody; operate on verified read-only working copies and avoid altering original evidence.

nodes.title: DNS query analysis & DGA detection
nodes.goal: Detect algorithmically generated domains (DGA), high-frequency NXDOMAIN queries, fast-flux DNS, and DNS tunneling.
nodes.why: DNS is the primary mechanism for C2 domain resolution, malware rendezvous, and covert data exfiltration.
checklist: Extract all DNS queries and responses ('tshark -Y dns -T fields -e dns.qry.name -e dns.a').
Calculate Shannon entropy on domain names to identify algorithmically generated domains (DGA).
Analyze NXDOMAIN response ratios to detect dead C2 fallbacks and domain generation sweeps.
Inspect high-frequency TXT and NULL record lookups for DNS tunneling indicators.
lookFor: High-entropy subdomains, repetitive NXDOMAIN bursts, abnormal TXT record payload lengths, and dynamic DNS providers.
nodes.record: Record dns query analysis & dga detection inputs, source locators, original timestamps and offsets, tool/version, settings, outputs, validation, errors, limitations, and hashes.
cautions: Maintain chain of custody; operate on verified read-only working copies and avoid altering original evidence.

findings.title: Suspicious DGA or C2 domain identified

nodes.title: Detect command & control (C2) beaconing patterns
nodes.goal: Isolate recurring periodic network requests, uniform delta intervals, jitter patterns, and persistent HTTP/HTTPS connections.
nodes.why: C2 implants communicate with controllers on predictable intervals; isolating beacons exposes active backdoors and infrastructure.
checklist: Extract session timestamps between specific IP pairs and calculate inter-arrival delta intervals.
Identify regular periodicity (e.g. connection every 60s ± 10% jitter).
Inspect HTTP User-Agent headers, URI structures, and cookie formats for known C2 framework signatures (Cobalt Strike, Mythic, Sliver).
Analyze persistent TCP streams with minimal data exchange (heartbeat / keep-alive traffic).
lookFor: Low-variance connection intervals, static User-Agents, repetitive URI parameters, and unusual HTTP POST heartbeat bodies.
nodes.record: Record detect command & control (c2) beaconing patterns inputs, source locators, original timestamps and offsets, tool/version, settings, outputs, validation, errors, limitations, and hashes.
cautions: Maintain chain of custody; operate on verified read-only working copies and avoid altering original evidence.

nodes.title: Extract transferred payloads & stream objects
nodes.goal: Carve transferred files, staged binaries, and malicious payloads from unencrypted HTTP, SMB, and FTP streams.
nodes.why: Reconstructing transferred payloads enables malware analysis and identifies exactly what scripts or data crossed the network boundary.
checklist: Export HTTP stream objects using 'tshark --export-objects http,./exported'.
Extract files transferred over SMB/SMB2 using 'tshark --export-objects smb,./exported_smb'.
Reassemble raw TCP streams using Wireshark / TShark follow stream functionality.
Compute SHA-256 hashes of all carved objects and check against threat intelligence databases.
lookFor: Downloaded executables (.exe, .dll), scripts (.ps1, .vbs, .sh), document droppers (.docx, .xlsm), and staged archives.
nodes.record: Record extract transferred payloads & stream objects inputs, source locators, original timestamps and offsets, tool/version, settings, outputs, validation, errors, limitations, and hashes.
cautions: Maintain chain of custody; operate on verified read-only working copies and avoid altering original evidence.

findings.title: Executable payload carved from network stream

nodes.title: Inspect TLS handshakes, JA3/JA4 fingerprints & certificates
nodes.goal: Analyze ClientHello packets, JA3/JA4 TLS client signatures, self-signed certificates, and SNI domain discrepancies.
nodes.why: Encrypted traffic hides packet payloads, but TLS negotiation parameters fingerprint client applications and malware families.
checklist: Extract TLS ClientHello cipher suites, extensions, elliptic curves, and point formats.
Compute and look up JA3/JA3S and JA4 hashes for suspicious client endpoints.
Extract server certificates, issuer authorities, validity dates, and subject names.
Compare Server Name Indication (SNI) against DNS lookups and destination IP WHOIS records.
lookFor: Known malware JA3 signatures, self-signed or expired certificates, domain fronting indicators, and mismatched SNI vs certificate subjects.
